segments.text: Hi, I'm Brunchandama. I'm a lead design engineer working on Millicode. So what is Millicode?
It basically is a form of microarchitecture that runs on IBMC. And by microarchitecture, I mean, there's a
layer
invisible layer between what we publish in the principles of operations and
another layer which is a microarchitecture. And
And the reason why we have that is because every generation of z, the microarchitecture changes.
However, what we publish in the principles of operation, that does not change. We add stuff,
we don't remove stuff. We add new instructions, we don't remove instructions. So an instruction
that we introduced 10 years ago, functionally it does the same thing, but microarchitecture,
really how we get to that answer is very different. And in Millicode, we make those changes so
that the operating system or the user of the program doesn't have to make those changes.
In addition to the instruction set, the implemented instruction set on the principle of operations,
Millicode is also involved in a few other key aspects of IBM Z. We do system initialization,
which basically means you pull an on the system, going to the IML steps, initial machine load,
that's IML. Millicode is involved with virtualization. So you have a single resource, a system,
and you're going to divide it up into logical partitions and run different operating systems
in each partition. For that, to be possible, you need an instruction that's called
SIE or start interpretive execution, and that instruction is implemented in Millicode.
So that's Millicode in a nutshell. As you can see, the things that we do on the system is
important, especially for recovery, for availability, and for serviceability. I've been enjoying
my work in Millicode, and it's been fun joining so far. Thank you.
